estimates.narrative: Using the IOM Missing Migrants reference class, the record start to 2026 with about 606 deaths by February strongly signals a high chance of reaching 1,000 deaths before May, assuming no major rescue or policy shifts. The final estimate weights pace most heavily, with SPR and SAR dynamics providing offsets; overall calibration yields a 98% posterior with narrow uncertainty.
summary: Early-2026 pace (~606 deaths by February) implies a high likelihood of surpassing 1,000 Mediterranean deaths by May if the pace persists.
Spring conditions could raise crossing opportunities, while SAR capacity and policy shifts could modestly dampen or amplify the trajectory.
Base-rate patterns and lack of a formal forecast model keep uncertainty but support a high-probability near-term crossing.

question: Will the IOM Missing Migrants Project record at least 1,000 Mediterranean migrant deaths in 2026 before May 2026?
summary: Ensemble aggregate is 97%, reflecting strong consensus across outside-view, inside-view, and contrarian estimates.
Early 2026 data show roughly 606 deaths by late February, suggesting a high base-rate risk of reaching 1,000 by May if the pace persists.
Adversarial objections highlight downward pressures (seasonality, policy/SAR changes) but are not sufficient to overturn the high base probability given historical patterns.
No systematic bias detected in the ensemble that would warrant adjustment; the final probability remains anchored at the ensemble estimate with a narrow uncertainty range.

justification.critique_assessment: The objections identify plausible near-term downward pressures but do not reveal a fundamental bias in the ensemble; pace signals and historical patterns remain the dominant drivers.

causal-factors.name: Pace of deaths early 2026
causal-factors.rationale: 606 deaths or missing migrants by February 2026 indicate a record-start, making it plausible that totals could exceed 1,000 by May if the pace persists.

causal-factors.name: Spring sea conditions and seasonal access
causal-factors.rationale: Calmer spring seas typically enable more crossings, increasing exposure to fatal incidents and raising the near-term risk of reaching the threshold.

causal-factors.name: Search-and-rescue (SAR) capacity and safe disembarkation
causal-factors.rationale: Sustained or expanded rescue capacity and safer disembarkation reduce deaths, potentially dampening the upward trajectory.

causal-factors.name: Policy crackdown and deterrence effects on routes
causal-factors.rationale: Crackdowns and tighter controls can push migrants toward more dangerous routes, increasing fatalities.

causal-factors.name: Data gaps and reporting lags (undercount risk)
causal-factors.rationale: Under-counting or late reporting could mean higher final totals than currently observed, supporting a higher end-of-spring total.

causal-factors.name: Pace of Mediterranean deaths in early 2026 (through February)
causal-factors.rationale: Approximately 606 deaths or missing persons were reported by late February 2026, marking a record-start to the year; if this pace continues, reaching or exceeding 1,000 deaths by May becomes highly probable.

causal-factors.name: Persistent or rising migrant flows via the Central Mediterranean
causal-factors.rationale: Early-2026 tolls echo ongoing high flow and risk in the Central Mediterranean; historical totals (e.g., 2025 Mediterranean deaths around 2,108) suggest that continued flows elevate the probability of surpassing 1,000 deaths by spring.

causal-factors.name: Regulatory and political restrictions on rescue operations (NGO SAR, coast guard coordination)
causal-factors.rationale: Policy constraints that limit rescue capacity can increase fatalities, pushing the likelihood of reaching 1,000 deaths higher.

causal-factors.name: Variability and potential changes in search-and-rescue capacity
causal-factors.rationale: Any expansion or improvement in SAR capacity and safe-migration pathways could mitigate fatalities and reduce the chance of surpassing 1,000 deaths by May.

synthesis: The first months of 2026 show a record pace that makes crossing 1,000 deaths by May plausible. While there are downward risks, the historical context and current pace support keeping the ensemble-projected probability near 0.97, with a tight range reflecting uncertainty about unfolding seasonal and policy factors.
